title: NeoRadar radars dataset
description: datasets/radars.json: the radar stations whose coverage the client simulates, in the shape of EuroScope's ESE RADAR2 line. Each station carries up to three sensors, primary, secondary and Mode S, each with a range, an antenna altitude and a cone-of-silence slope. A target is seen by a sensor when it is within the range and not inside the cone above the antenna, that is when its height above the antenna is at most the slope times its distance. Out of every sensor's coverage a target draws nothing at all; inside primary coverage only it reads PrimaryOnly whatever its transponder does; without Mode S coverage there is no Mode S identification. Absent file means no simulation: every sensor sees everything, which is the existing behaviour. HOLE blocks are holes: inside the polygon a sensor kind has no coverage below its floor, whatever the stations say. Per package, never global.

rawVideo.description: What SIZES a synthesised primary return at this station, as against the sensors above, which decide whether one is seen at all. Written by `neoradar-cli topsky-convert` out of the vAcc's own TopSkyRadars.txt and merged onto the station by name, then by position within 500 m. The client picks the FIRST station whose positions prefix matches the view's login callsign, exactly as TopSky does, and a view matching no station draws the return life size with the explainer saying why. Absent block means today's behaviour: the return is the size of the aircraft.

beamwidthDeg.description: Half-power beamwidth in degrees. A target is drawn twice this wide in azimuth, so the return grows with range: an aircraft 20 NM from a 1.25 degree head smears about 0.87 NM across, which is why an en-route raw video picture shows arcs rather than aeroplanes.

pulseWidthUs.description: Transmitted pulse width in microseconds. A target is drawn 0.08 NM deep in range per microsecond, and that depth does NOT grow with range.

maxAngleDeg.description: Elevation above which the head sees nothing: the cone of silence over the antenna.

positions.description: Login callsign prefixes this station serves, matched from the start of the callsign. One station per login, first match in file order wins, so order the stations from the most specific prefix to the least.

antennaAltitudeFt.description: Antenna altitude AMSL in feet. The ESE sensors carry their own; this is what a station present only in the TopSky file has.

minRangeNm.description: Inside this range nothing is detected.

maxRangeNm.description: Outside this range nothing is detected. The ESE sensors carry their own ranges and those decide coverage; this one is the TopSky file's own figure, kept so the two can be compared.

antennaAltitudeFt.description: Antenna altitude in feet, the apex of the cone of silence.

coneSlopeFtPerNm.description: Cone of silence: a target more than this many feet above the antenna per nautical mile of distance is not seen. EuroScope's files carry 3100. 0 or absent means no cone.

latitude.description: WGS84 degrees, north positive. Unlike the package GeoJSON these are degrees, as the ESE line has them.

hole.description: An ESE HOLE block. Inside the polygon, each sensor kind that names a floor has no coverage below it; a kind with no floor is unaffected.

primaryBelowFt.description: No primary return below this altitude in feet inside the polygon.

secondaryBelowFt.description: No secondary return below this altitude in feet inside the polygon.

modeSBelowFt.description: No Mode S return below this altitude in feet inside the polygon.

polygon.description: Vertices as [latitude, longitude] in WGS84 degrees, the station order, not GeoJSON's. The ring closes itself.
